anatomy.flutter: Disabled is a StatelessWidget: TweenAnimationBuilder->Opacity->IgnorePointer wraps `child`, then MouseRegion+GestureDetector, then a conditional outer Tooltip(label: reason) only when reason is non-empty; tree shape is stable per call site.
anatomy.web: Disabled renders a <span data-slot="disabled"> around the cloned child plus, only when hasReason, a sr-only <span id={reasonId}> and a Popover/PopoverTrigger(Button icon-xs)/PopoverContent beside (not wrapping) the child.
anatomy.note: Flutter wraps the whole subtree in a hover/long-press Tooltip; web deliberately avoids Tooltip and adds a separate focusable icon-button+Popover beside the child so the reason is reachable by keyboard and touch, per the file's own 'THE REASON SURFACE' doc comment. This is the documented, correct divergence, not a defect.

api.flutter: Disabled({required disabled, required child, reason, onDisabledTap, blockPointer=true, duration}) — Button composes it directly, passing its own measured spring via `duration: transition` (button.dart:1161-1164).
api.web: DisabledProps { disabled, reason?, mode?: "native"|"aria" = "native", onDisabledAttempt?, children: ReactElement, className? } — Button never composes Disabled; it sets `disabled:opacity-50` itself per the file doc comment's 'READ THIS FIRST'.
api.note: Flutter centralizes fade+pointer-block+duration in Disabled and every control (e.g. Button) wraps itself in it; web keeps native disabled native on the control and Disabled only adds the reason surface, with a mode flag (native/aria) that Flutter has no equivalent prop for — that behaviour is instead hand-coded per call site in menu.dart's MenuItem row (blockPointer:false, onTap gated by `enabled`).

states.flutter: TweenAnimationBuilder tweens opacity between 1 and SurfaceOpacity.disabled with MotionCurves.emphasized over MotionDurations.fast (or the passed duration), and MouseRegion swaps cursor to SystemMouseCursors.basic while disabled.
states.web: data-disabled attribute toggles on the wrapper span and `disabled && "cursor-not-allowed"` is applied via cn(); the reason trigger Button toggles disabled/aria-hidden/tabIndex between the enabled and disabled states.
states.note: Same two-state model (rest vs disabled) with a fade/cursor pairing on both sides; the fade is a spring/curve animation in Flutter and an instant class-attribute swap plus the target control's own CSS transition on web.

disabled.flutter: Disabled itself performs the fade (Opacity/TweenAnimationBuilder) and the pointer block (IgnorePointer(ignoring: disabled && blockPointer)) for every control that composes it, e.g. Button always wraps itself in Disabled(duration: transition, reason: widget.disabledReason).
disabled.web: The doc comment's 'READ THIS FIRST' states most disabled controls need only native `disabled:opacity-50` and no wrapper at all; Disabled never sets/clears the native `disabled` attribute and is reached for only when a reason+recovery path is worth surfacing.
disabled.note: Flutter's Disabled is the one mechanism every fadeable control composes; web's Disabled is opt-in and additive, explicitly not the mechanism for the fade/pointer-block itself (that stays in each base component's own Tailwind classes) — a documented, correct architectural split for keeping native disabled semantics native.

interaction.flutter: GestureDetector wraps the whole result with HitTestBehavior.opaque and onTap: disabled ? onDisabledTap : null, so any pointer tap anywhere on a disabled Disabled fires onDisabledTap even with no reason set.
interaction.web: In mode="aria", Disabled wraps the child's onClick/onKeyDown (Enter/Space) with preventDefault/stopPropagation and calls onDisabledAttempt; in the default native mode there is no wrapper-level click interception at all, because native `disabled` consumes the event before any handler can observe it.
interaction.note: Flutter can always observe an attempted tap on a disabled area via onDisabledTap; web's native mode cannot by design (documented: 'native disabled blocks the underlying control before any handler could observe the attempt'), so onDisabledAttempt only fires from the aria path or from the reason trigger's own click — a real, intentional browser-semantics constraint, not a missed port.

semantics.flutter: Disabled adds no Semantics node of its own; reason discovery is only the Tooltip(label: reason, hidden: !disabled), which tooltip.dart shows is hover/long-press triggered, not a permanent screen-reader description.
semantics.web: Reason text sits in a permanently visually-hidden <span id={reasonId}> merged into the child's aria-describedby via mergeIds(), so a screen-reader user hears it on landing on the control without opening anything, plus a click/tap/Enter/Space-reachable Popover with aria-label="Why this is disabled".
semantics.note: Web does strictly more accessibility work than Flutter here: an always-on aria-describedby path plus a click/touch/keyboard-reachable Popover, versus Flutter's hover/long-press-only Tooltip with no persistent description — the web mechanism is the correct one given the file's touch/keyboard reachability requirement.
